evidence.note: Wrote an initial Triton kernel, then a separate reference.py oracle, loaded TodoWrite to structure milestones, and wrote/ran a correctness test — establishing distinct correctness-checking phase before any perf work.

Fixed the mask/core-op correctness (debug_mask, edits, re-run correctness), updated TodoWrite, and only then wrote bench.py and benchmarked — a clean correctness→latency transition, evidence of ordered phases.

Correctness bugs (failing element at step 514) surfaced deep inside the long optimization phase, showing the correctness gate was not firmly closed before perf tuning began — the exit criterion for 'correct' was loose.
Comprehensive multi-seed strict tests across the 10 grader shapes only ran near the very end, so full-domain correctness verification was deferred rather than gating the optimization work.

reasoning: The agent exhibited clearly separated phases — reference oracle, Triton correctness, then latency tuning — with TodoWrite used to mark milestones, matching anchor 5 and edging to 6 because of the explicit reference+todo scaffolding and risk-first fix of the core contraction/mask. It falls well short of anchor 8 because there was no explicit 'matches reference within 2e-2 on all shapes before perf' exit criterion: optimization started after only basic correctness, correctness bugs were chased mid-optimization (step 514), and full-domain multi-seed verification was deferred to the end.
